answer: One concrete mechanism: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because horizon only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, kernel is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any plume approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
